persona_bot.summary: PersonaAI (persona_bot) is a Node/Express chat companion with six switchable personas (boyfriend "Bae", best friend, study mate, teacher, therapist, motivator) that chats in Hinglish with one named user over a WhatsApp-style web UI, remembers her across sessions in a JSON file, and can answer over uploaded documents via a small RAG pipeline. Prompts live in persona/*.js (per-persona system prompts), personalities.js (a mood layer rotated every 5 turns), profile.js and summary.js (profile-extractor and summariser prompts), assembled by promptBuilder.js and sent to Groq (openai/gpt-oss-120b) through llm.js; persistent memory is read and written by memory.js to ./memory.json.

Open-LLM-VTuber.summary: Open-LLM-VTuber is a self-hosted voice-interactive AI companion with a Live2D avatar: the person talks (voice or text) to a configurable persona that answers with speech and animated expressions, in single, group or livestream modes. Prompts live in config_templates/conf.default.yaml (persona_prompt plus a tool_prompts list), characters/*.yaml (alternative personas) and prompts/utils/*.txt (appended system-prompt fragments and the proactive-speak prompt); the frontend is an empty git submodule, so only the backend was swept.

open-recommender.summary: open-recommender is a TypeScript/Python monorepo (Express + tRPC + Prisma server, React client, CLI prompt library, Python RAG and twscrape workers) that logs a person in with Twitter, scrapes their timeline with pooled operator accounts, has GPT-4 write a 500-word interest profile from it, has GPT-4 role-play the person to write research questions, searches YouTube/Metaphor, and ranks transcript chunks with a ColBERT reranker against those questions. Crisis: nothing; no chat surface and no screening of the notes box or custom query. Engagement: designed in. A cron re-runs the pipeline for every user every 48 hours and e-mails results with rotating marketing subjects and a 'Go to your feed' button; e-mail is hard-coded on at signup, in the cron and in manual requests, with no opt-out field, no unsubscribe link, and the policy's promised unsubscribe option does not exist. The feed is a Shorts-style autoplay queue and the homepage states that goal. The like signal enters at getUserContext.ts:260-269, where any timeline item not authored by the person is labelled a like (retweets at 270-279), rendered as 'Liked by ...' text, and summarized into the profile (recursiveTwitterSummarizer.ts:89, saga.ts:268). The profile is meant to reach query generation at saga.ts:307, but a 'typeof' bug passes the word 'string' instead of the text, so in the deployed pipeline only the Twitter bio and username drive the queries. Ranking (saga.ts:511, rag.ts:148) is semantic relevance to the questions, not predicted engagement; thumbs votes are stored and displayed with voter identity but never fed back; the 'follow to get clips they liked' promise has no pipeline code. Limits present: no e-mail when a run yields no clips, max 2 runs per user, and an anti-clickbait appraisal prompt that is CLI-only. Sycophancy: no agree/flatter instructions; a 'both sides' instruction is wired in and a be-critical appraisal prompt is not. Disclosure: a 'Why was this recommended?' dialog shows the generated profile and query and says the system created them, but no UI, e-mail or policy text says AI or LLM; only the README does, and the policy denies inferring characteristics. Memory: raw tweets, the AI-written profile, e-mail, votes and notes persist across sessions; profiles are public by default and readable by any logged-in user on the profile page; the pipeline starts inside the login callback with consent implied by policy; the only opt-out flag (useForRecommendations) is unreachable from the client and ignored by the pipeline; deletion exists only as a policy promise by e-mail and an admin wipe-all script.
